Hi Samir -- thanks, this is a great set of questions. Attached are two artifacts we prepare for customers responding to procurement/security RFPs: a short model inventory CSV and our operational "Pinning & Update Playbook." High-level answers below; the playbook and inventory have examples you can drop into your appendix.

Summary answers (short):
- Provenance: Every model in our catalog includes: model_name, upstream_origin (URL or package), upstream_license, model_digest (SHA256 over the shipped artifact), runtime-config (quantization/compile flags), and a curated provenance note that includes training commit or release tag when available. We capture this at onboarding and freeze the record for any pinned model.
- SBOM-like artifacts: Yes — our model_inventory.csv is effectively an SBOM for model artifacts (manifest entries and license metadata). For regulated customers we provide expanded archives that include checksums, build logs, and provenance attestations.
- Pinning & immutability: We support immutable model identifiers (e.g., model-id@sha256:<digest>) and recommend enterprises pin to the digest-based identifier for production. Pinning options:
  * Soft pin (version tag): points to a specific catalog version; can be updated via change-control.
  * Hard pin (digest): immutable; guarantees reproducible bits and execution behavior.
- Rollback & updates: Our platform supports automatic rollback to a prior digest in the event of a regression. We also support canary rollouts with observability gates (latency, token-level cost, quality regressions) and automated fallback to a pinned compatible variant if a new variant violates SLOs.
- License obligations: We publish upstream license metadata for each model. For licenses that carry compatibility obligations, our playbook outlines downstream obligations and offers templated notice language for customers. We do not relicense upstream models; we surface the obligations clearly and provide guidance for remediation (e.g., remove or replace components, or apply an allowed usage pattern).

Attachments included: model_inventory.csv (sample), pinning-playbook.pdf (playbook outline), redwood-soc2-evidence-stub.txt (pointer to SOC2 artifacts; full bundle available under NDA).

If helpful I can walk through the playbook with your SecOps team and show the console pin flows and rollback demo.
